verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is scheduled to return to Earth on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA’s Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down ... on Friday, April 10.'; R3: 'splashdown off the coast of San Diego, California on Friday, April 10'; R4: 'Orion will splash down ... on April 10'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state splashdown/return on Friday, April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule is expected to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splashdown off the coast of San Diego, California'; R4: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly confirm Pacific Ocean off San Diego.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule is expected to splash down at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splash down ... at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) on Friday, April 10'; R3: 'around 8:07 p.m.'; R4: '8:07 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and time zones match directly in R1.

verifications.claim: The total mission lasts about 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately 10-day journey'; R2: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II mission'; R3: '10-day lunar mission'; R4: '10-day mission'; R5: '10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources consistently describe the mission as approximately 10 days.

verifications.claim: The astronauts are on a four-day return journey following their lunar fly-by.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: Lunar flyby April 6, splashdown April 10 (4 days); R6: 'It will take them about four days to journey back'; R4: 'April 7-9: ... April 10: ... splashes down'
verifications.reasoning: Timeline from flyby (day 6, April 6) to splashdown (April 10) is 4 days; R6 explicitly states four days return.

verifications.claim: Recovery teams will retrieve the crew following splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'recovery teams will retrieve the crew using helicopters'; R3: 'the team will be flown via helicopter'; R4: 'recovery teams will retrieve the crew from Orion'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state recovery teams retrieve crew post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: Recovery teams will deliver the crew to a U.S. Navy ship for medical evaluation.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'deliver them to the USS John P. Murtha. Once aboard, the astronauts will undergo post-mission medical evaluations'; R3: 'flown ... to the USS John P. Murtha. They will then undergo post-flight medical evaluations'; R4: 'use helicopters to deliver them to a nearby ship. Once aboard, the astronauts will undergo post‑mission medical evaluations'
verifications.reasoning: Exact process described: delivery to Navy ship (USS John P. Murtha) for medical eval.
